messages:
maya: quick follow-up to the Quantized Attention RFC — want to capture implementation notes and open tradeoffs for FP8/INT8/INT4 + dequant fusion.

maya: TL;DR: fused dequant->matmul->softmax path looks promising for perf, but we need clear kernel API boundaries and a robust fallback story for numerical issues.

sam: +1. can you list the concrete perf targets and the expected memory savings?

maya: perf targets: 1) reduce token latency by ~10-30% vs unfused int8 path on A100; 2) reduce peak GPU memory for KV cache by ~20-50% depending on quant level. rough.

igor: details matter: FP8 accumulation vs fp16 accumulation, per-channel scales, and quant granularity (per-tensor vs per-channel) will change correctness and speed.

maya: agreed. proposing three supported quant modes initially: FP8 (E4M3), INT8 (symmetric per-channel), INT4 (per-tensor with scale table). mode selectable per-model at load time.

rachel: where does dequant happen? model loader or kernel? my vote: runtime should supply quant params (scales/zero points) and kernels accept quant pointers to avoid host-side copies.

sam: +1 to runtime-provided params. but kernel API must be simple: pointers to qdata, scale, optional bias, and a flag for fused_dequant=true.

maya: propose API sketch (pseudo):

```
// fused attention kernel call
fused_attn_qkv_f32(
  uint8_t* q_qv_buf, // quantized QKV
  float* q_scale,     // per-channel or per-tensor
  int8_t* q_zero_pt,  // optional
  uint8_t* k_v_buf,   // quantized KV for cache
  float* kv_scale,
  void* kv_cache_out, // preallocated dequantized cache (optional)
  attn_params_t* params
);
```

maya: kernel will do: dequant(Q)->matmul->softmax->matmul and optionally write dequantized KV to cache if downstream requires FP32/FP16 accumulation.

igor: two big choices: 1) write dequantized KV to cache (memory hit) vs keep KV quantized and dequant on the fly. 2) do activation-level fusion vs per-op kernels.

rachel: on-the-fly dequant reduces memory but increases compute per-token. for long context (64k-ish) quantized KV on-device is huge win. maybe hybrid: write dequant when model requests high-precision (few layers) else keep quantized. need a policy.

sam: policy should be config-driven with fallback heuristics: if numerical instability detected (NaNs, >epsilon divergence from fp32 baseline in eval samples) switch to dequant-by-default for that model/version.

maya: good. also we need calibration metadata per model: scale tensors, min/max ranges, plus an eval prompt set to validate numerical drift. store these in model manifest.

igor: about accumulation precision: use fp16 accumulation for int8 matmuls and fp32 for fp8? what's the plan? fp8->acc fp16 may be unstable for some weights.

maya: initial plan: fp8 mode uses fp32 accumulation, int8 uses fp16 accumulation (if hardware supports TF32/FP16 fused ops fallback to fp32 otherwise). will add per-model override in manifest.

rachel: testing: need microbench harness that runs token loops with KV cache sizes 1024/4096/65536 tokens and measures latency, tail latency, and memory. ci-bot should fail if relative token output divergence > threshold.

ml-ci-bot: noted. I can add a quant-attn perf suite to CI with synthetic workloads. will run on A100, H100, and V100 (if available).

sam: what about dequant fusion safety net? suggestion: kernel returns a diagnostics struct (max_abs_error_estimate, overflow_flag, detour_hit) that runtime logs and triggers rollback to safe path.

maya: yes. diagnostics will be part of kernel ABI. runtime collects stats and can trigger canary rollouts.

igor: implementation detail: keep kernel ABI minimal and forward-compatible: pointer + strides + metadata blob (opaque) where we can add fields. avoids frequent ABI churn.

rachel: also think about memory pinning and cudaHostRegister for zero-copy if runtime wants to stream quantized weights from pinned buffers. impacts page-locked memory usage. call out in docs.

maya: rollout plan: 1) implement fused kernel in eng-runtime dev branch, 2) land INT8 path first, benchmark and CI, 3) add FP8 after numeric validation, 4) INT4 as experimental. enable behind feature flag scoped to Dedicated clusters and internal customers initially.

sam: can we get quick prototype numbers? even microbench on tiny model (1.3B) to validate perf direction.

maya: I'll do a prototype this week. expected perf wins: ~1.15x-1.35x latency for INT8 fused on A100, and 30-45% KV memory reduction. will report back with numbers.

rachel: action items: @maya prototype + perf numbers; @igor design ABI docs; @sam create canary rollout plan + feature flag; @ml-ci-bot add perf/regression suite.

maya: thanks. will post a follow-up doc with ABI sketch and benchmark table. :thumbsup:

deploy-bot: scheduled canary job created: quant-attn-proto-canary (cluster: devoted-gpus).

maya: added a short note in RFC thread with links to prototype branch and a small notebook for reproducing perf tests: https://git.redwood/proj/quant-attn/proto

sam: nice. one more thing — license/third-party kernels? if we pull in vendor kernels for fp8, make sure license compatible.

maya: noted. we'll vet licenses.

igor: small nit: document the fallback cost in SLO terms (e.g., “if we fallback to fp32, expect 2x token cost and +40ms median latency for 8k context”). helps product decide rollout.

maya: good point. I'll add SLO impact estimates to the follow-up doc.

rachel: :eyes: excited to see numbers.

maya: last: thinking about metrics to expose in Console — per-model quant mode, dequant-fusion enabled, kernel diagnostics (error rate, fallback count), and memory saving estimates. this will help customers choose.

sam: perfect. ok I think that's a solid plan.

maya: thanks all — closing thread, will post the writeup later today.
